messages.subject: LQ factorization in Nimble

I am fairly new at using Nimble, but I'd like to use it to estimate a factor model we're currently working on. In our factor modeling we have a loadings matrix (matrix of weights) that connects the outcomes to the factors. In our case, this loadings matrix is a sparse matrix with some none zero elements for which we have priors. What I'd like to accomplish is to decompose the loadings matrix into L and Q matrices and use L to fit the factor model. The code I wrote (given below the error message) errors out when I run the runMCMC function with the error message included below. It looks like that maybe my nimble Functions are not written correctly. I was hoping that I could get  some help on to fix this issue. 

Thank you very much!
Eva

Hi Eva,

I don't think you need `nimbleRcall` at all here. The case you would need `nimbleRcall` is when you want to use some functionality in R that nimble can't compile.
Here you are writing nimbleFunctions to do the QR calculation and nimble will just compile those nimbleFunctions. So if you just remove `cNimQR.Q` and  `cNimQR.R` and in your model code call `nimQR.Q` and `nimQR.R`, it should work.

On an efficiency note, if you start to work with bigger matrices, you will probably want to have a single function that returns both Q and R together rather than doing the same calculation twice. It's a bit of a hassle to do this because a nimble model can work with lists, but you could have a `nimQR` nimbleFunction that returns Q and R as part of a larger matrix (e.g., in your example you could have the result be a 10x6 matrix) and then in your model code extract the two pieces as needed (the first 4 rows and the last 6 rows in your example).

-chris

I don't think you need `nimbleRcall` at all here. The case you would need `nimbleRcall` is when you want to use some functionality in R that nimble can't compile.

On an efficiency note, if you start to work with bigger matrices, you will probably want to have a single function that returns both Q and R together rather than doing the same calculation twice.
